title: Largest Prime from Consecutive Prime Sum
summary: Given an integer n, find the largest prime number less than or equal to n that can be formed by summing one or more consecutive prime numbers starting from 2.
statement: Given an integer n, find the largest prime number less than or equal to n that can be formed by summing one or more consecutive prime numbers starting from 2. If no such prime exists, return 0.
constraints: Candidates are prefix sums 2, 2+3, 2+3+5, and so on.
Return the largest candidate no greater than n that is prime, or zero when none exists.
hints: Only prefix sums of the prime sequence beginning at two are eligible.
Use a sieve through n, scan primes in order, accumulate their sum, and record sums that are themselves prime.
Stop when the running sum exceeds n and return the last recorded value.
The scan generates every allowed consecutive-prime prefix exactly once and the sieve tests primality exactly.
editorial: The scan generates every allowed consecutive-prime prefix exactly once and the sieve tests primality exactly.

tests.explanation: Prime prefix sums two, five, and seventeen are at most twenty, so return seventeen.
The first prime prefix sum is two itself.
